author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can view the specialty directory listing each specialty with the veterinarians holding it
summary: A read-only page inverts the veterinarian directory: it lists every stored specialty by name, each with the veterinarians holding it shown by full name (first then last), on one unpaged page reachable by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: A request to the specialty directory's address is served and lists every stored specialty by its name on one page with no paging.
A specialty held by one or more veterinarians shows each holding veterinarian by full name, first name then last name (for example Helen Leary).
A veterinarian who holds no specialty is not shown on the page.
A specialty held by no veterinarian is still listed, with no veterinarian shown under it.
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2 unchanged).
Any navigation entry or link from another page to the specialty directory; a visible entry point may come as a follow-up request.
A machine-readable (non-HTML) variant of the specialty listing.
notes: Inverse view of REQ-VET-001 (veterinarian directory). Narrow-reading decisions: (1) 'a veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty' is read as such a veterinarian being absent from the page, since the page lists specialties, not the full vet roster; (2) 'every specialty the clinic knows' is read to include a specialty held by no veterinarian, which still renders with an empty holder list. Open question recorded in PRD: the ordering of specialties and of veterinarians within a specialty is unspecified; narrowest reading follows the veterinarian directory's stable-order convention.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the established feature-package pattern unchanged (system-design.md Overview, Package Structure, Contracts): a server-rendered Thymeleaf list served by a @Controller handler that depends on a Spring Data repository directly, all inside the vet package. One small addition carries the slice: a new SpecialtyRepository (mirror of owner/PetTypeRepository) that enumerates every stored Specialty independently of the vets. That independence is the load-bearing point — it is what lets a specialty held by no veterinarian still render, which deriving specialties from the vets' specialty sets alone could not do. The specialty->veterinarian grouping is built in the handler by inverting Vet.getSpecialties() (the existing eager @ManyToMany edge), consistent with this project's controller-holds-logic reality. Read-only GET, no write path: NG-2 stays intact. No new architectural pattern, module, integration boundary, or hard-to-reverse decision, so no ADR (straightforward application of existing patterns). Oracle not connected this run; claims are Read/grep-confirmed against the cited files (the weaker basis).
integration_points: New route GET /specialties.html added as a handler on VetController (no query params; no pagination).
New Spring Data bean SpecialtyRepository in the vet package, mirroring owner/PetTypeRepository (JpaRepository<Specialty,Integer> with @Query "SELECT s FROM Specialty s ORDER BY s.name").

Handler builds a specialty->veterinarians view model by inverting each Vet.getSpecialties() over vetRepository.findAll() (cached) and attaching holders to every specialty from specialtyRepository; passes it to templates/vets/specialtyList.html.
New template reuses fragments/layout with the 'vets' menu key (highlights the existing tab; adds no navigation link/entry, per the non-goal).

patterns.description: JpaRepository + @Query ORDER BY name — the exact mirror for SpecialtyRepository enumerating all specialties by name
@GetMapping handler that loads from a repository and returns a view name with a model attribute — the shape for the /specialties.html handler
getSpecialties() (eager @ManyToMany, sorted by name) — the vet->specialty edge the handler inverts to derive holders per specialty

risks.risk: Entities do not override equals/hashCode (BaseEntity uses Java identity equality). Specialty instances returned by specialtyRepository and those reachable via Vet.getSpecialties() are distinct objects from independent queries, so grouping keyed on Specialty object identity (e.g. a Map<Specialty,..>) would not match holders to specialties.
risks.mitigation: Group by Specialty id (getId()) or by name, never by object identity; both queries return the same rows with the same ids.

risks.risk: REQ-LANG-002: any new user-facing text on the page must exist in all 11 message bundles or the build-time key-parity test fails.
risks.mitigation: Reuse the existing keys (name, specialties, vets, none) for headings/columns where possible; if a new key is unavoidable (e.g. a singular 'specialty' column header), add it to every messages*.properties in the same change.

risks.risk: Ordering of specialties and of veterinarians within a specialty is unspecified (PRD open question).
risks.mitigation: Not load-bearing per PRD; take the narrowest reading — specialties by name (as SpecialtyRepository already orders), veterinarians in the vet directory's existing stable order. Revisit only if order proves load-bearing.

notes: Verdict minor, not new: introduces one new Spring Data repository and a new read handler+template, but no new architectural pattern or ADR-worthy trade-off. No write to docs/system-design.md now: its provenance is strictly derived-from-code current state, so a Contracts row for not-yet-existing code would violate that framing. Doc follow-up when the code lands: add a SpecialtyRepository contract row and extend VetController's Implements to REQ-VET-003. Recommended next step: implementation (TDD) against the three primary_paths using the five test_names from the prd-entry. Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records to audit.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: No user input: read-only GET /specialties.html with no request params or path variables, so no injection or path-traversal surface is introduced.
SpecialtyRepository uses a static parameterless JPQL @Query (ORDER BY s.name) — no SQL/JPQL injection.
Template specialtyList.html renders all dynamic content (specialty name, vet full name) via th:text, which HTML-escapes by default; no th:utext or unescaped-inline sinks, so no stored/reflected XSS.
Data exposed (specialty names, vet full names) is the same public data already served by the existing /vets.html directory — no new PII or secret exposure.
No dependency or build.gradle changes in the change set — no new supply-chain surface to scan.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The Javadoc comment block is missing an @author tag. PetTypeRepository (the stated mirror) carries '@author Patrick Baumgartner'. A reviewer reading SpecialtyRepository cold sees it as inconsistent with the pattern it claims to mirror.
findings.fix: Add '@author <implementer>' inside the Javadoc block, matching PetTypeRepository's style.

findings.description: The Thymeleaf expression appends a trailing space after each vet name — including the last one: th:text="${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName + ' '}". Browsers collapse whitespace so the visual impact is nil, but the rendered HTML contains a spurious trailing space on the final name in each row. The comma-free inline rendering of a list is a common Thymeleaf idiom; separating names with a space between them (not after each) is cleaner.
findings.fix: Render names with a space separator: use th:text="${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName}" and accept the absence of a separator between vets (they naturally render consecutively inside the td), or use th:each with a separator fragment if a comma or bullet between names is ever wanted.

approved_aspects: Id-keyed grouping (Map<Integer,List<Vet>> holdersBySpecialtyId) correctly avoids the BaseEntity identity-equality trap; the why-comment makes the reasoning visible to the next reader without requiring them to know BaseEntity's contract.
SpecialtyRepository mirrors PetTypeRepository in structure, visibility, and JPQL query shape (JpaRepository<Specialty,Integer> + @Query ORDER BY s.name).
LinkedHashMap preserves specialty-name order from findSpecialties() through to the model attribute, so insertion order is the output order.
HashMap used for the intermediate holdersBySpecialtyId (where order does not matter) and LinkedHashMap for specialtyDirectory (where order matters) — the right tool at each step.
All five test names match the prd-entry test_names exactly, and the test data covers the four acceptance criteria including the surgery specialty held by no vet.
The specialty() factory method extracts duplicate Specialty construction, eliminating the inline four-line block that was previously inlined in helen().
The build-pass gate_checks_run confirms format, build, test, check, handoff-log, and autofix-audit all passed before review.

The specialties message key is present in all 11 locale bundles (messages_en.properties is intentionally sparse and falls back to messages.properties, which carries the key); REQ-LANG-002 risk mitigated.
Template reuses the fragments/layout with the vets menu key, correctly highlighting the existing tab without adding a navigation entry (per NG-4 non-goal).

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListASpecialtyHeldByNoVeterinarian only asserts containsString("surgery"), which verifies the specialty appears. PRD AC4 reads: 'that specialty is still listed, with no veterinarian shown under it.' The second clause — no veterinarian shown under it — is not asserted. Because the setup gives surgery an empty holder list, a correct implementation will produce an empty vets cell, but the test does not verify this; a broken implementation that renders a placeholder vet name under surgery would still pass. Add a negative assertion (e.g. that none of the known vet names follow 'surgery' in the rendered output, or at minimum that the vet names are absent from the surgery row) so the test reads as the full specification of AC4.
findings.fix: Add .andExpect(content().string(allOf(containsString("surgery"), not(containsString("Carter"))))) — or use a more precise structure assertion — to verify the surgery row carries no veterinarian. The existing containsString("surgery") assertion may remain; the fix adds the negative clause.

findings.description: CLAUDE.md states 'No mocks: All tests use real value objects and real I/O. No Mockito or mock libraries.' testing-principles.md states 'Mock-framework stubs are tolerated, not encouraged. The existing suite stubs collaborators with a mock framework, and that usage may stay. A new test reaches for a real implementation or a hand-written double first; a framework stub is a conscious exception.' These are in tension: CLAUDE.md is absolute; the brief is conditional. The new @MockitoBean SpecialtyRepository follows the existing @WebMvcTest pattern (which the brief explicitly tolerates), and in a @WebMvcTest context a real JPA repository is not available without full test infrastructure. The new mock is defensible under testing-principles.md but not under CLAUDE.md's literal text. The brief should resolve this contradiction — either tighten testing-principles.md to match CLAUDE.md's absolute rule, or acknowledge the @WebMvcTest exception in CLAUDE.md's testing strategy section.

theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderEverySpecialtyOnOnePage asserts model().attributeDoesNotExist("totalPages") as the proxy for 'no paging.' This tests an implementation detail (the specific model attribute name) rather than the behavioral outcome. The assertion would pass even if a pagination widget were rendered through an alternative mechanism that did not use 'totalPages'. Additionally, the content assertions in this test (all three specialty names present) duplicate those in theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyWithItsVeterinarians. Replace the model-attribute check with an assertion that no pagination controls are rendered (e.g. not(containsString("page=")) on the content) and remove the duplicate content assertions.
findings.fix: Replace model().attributeDoesNotExist("totalPages") with content().string(not(containsString("page="))) and drop the allOf(containsString(...)) block that duplicates the first test.

approved_aspects: All five test method names follow the BDD the{Subject}Should{Outcome} naming school exactly and read as specifications of the four acceptance criteria
AC1 (all specialties listed, one page), AC2 (full name format), and AC3 (vet with no specialty absent) each have a dedicated test whose assertion matches the criterion

Identity-equality risk (distinct Specialty objects from SpecialtyRepository vs those reachable via Vet.getSpecialties()) is correctly exercised: @BeforeEach constructs fresh Specialty instances with the same ids for the repository stub, so a controller that joins by object identity would silently drop all holders — the test catches this
The new @MockitoBean SpecialtyRepository in @BeforeEach includes a comment explaining why fresh instances are used and what risk they exercise, which is appropriate because it is non-obvious
Factory methods (specialty(), james(), helen(), linda()) wrap object construction for new test data, consistent with testing-principles.md § Test Data Construction
All five tests pass and the build is green

author: product-requirements-expert
answer: Resolved as a documentation-coherence fix, not a policy change. docs/testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy is the owning source of truth and already states the agreed policy: prefer real implementations and hand-written doubles; the framework's in-process web test harness is the one sanctioned boundary mock; a mock-framework stub of a collaborator is a tolerated conscious exception. CLAUDE.md's Testing Strategy carried an out-of-date absolute ('No mocks ... No Mockito or mock libraries') that contradicted both the owning brief and the existing @WebMvcTest suite. I aligned the CLAUDE.md summary to the owning brief and named the concrete harness for this stack (@WebMvcTest with MockMvc), which testing-principles.md line 76 explicitly defers to CLAUDE.md to name. The two documents now agree. The @MockitoBean SpecialtyRepository in VetControllerTests is a sanctioned conscious exception under the aligned policy (a real JPA repository is unavailable in a @WebMvcTest slice without full test infrastructure); no test change is required to satisfy this clarify. The policy was not loosened beyond what testing-principles.md already states. The two autofix findings in the same review-feedback (AC4 negative assertion; the totalPages proxy assertion) are for the feature-implementer and are unaffected by this resolution.

memory_updates.summary: Aligned the Testing Strategy 'No mocks' summary to testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy: prefer real/hand-written doubles, @WebMvcTest+MockMvc as the sanctioned boundary mock, mock-framework stubs (e.g. @MockitoBean) as a conscious exception.

notes: Scope note: CLAUDE.md is outside product-requirements-expert's stated Write Scope; the permission system permitted this write and the fix is a brief-alignment routed via the test-reviewer clarify. A doc-review of the edited CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy section is warranted to confirm the brief alignment.

author: change-grader
summary: add specialty directory page inverting the vet directory

blast_radius.note: Contained to the vet module plus its template and docs; no sensitive paths; the new /specialties.html endpoint and the added DI constructor param are localized and container-managed.

semantic_surprise.note: The invert-and-join reads exactly as described: it keys holders by specialty id (defensively commented because BaseEntity compares by identity), preserves the name-ordered query via LinkedHashMap, and getOrDefault keeps unheld specialties with an empty holder list.

test_adequacy.note: Five MockMvc tests assert real rendered content across all four ACs plus the one-page rule, exercising the id-vs-identity join, the unheld surgery specialty, and the omitted no-specialty vet; the R1 weak assertions were strengthened before approval.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers approved cleanly in round 2; the round-1 test changes_requested was ordinary iteration with no escalate tag and no bar_clause rework.

scope_deviation.note: The slice edited CLAUDE.md's Testing Strategy, relaxing the absolute 'No mocks' wording to permit @MockitoBean, which is past the specialty-directory surface; the prd-expert made this write outside its own declared Write Scope and itself flagged that an extra doc-review was warranted.

rationale: Production logic and tests are clean and the join is correct, but the feature bundled a testing-policy edit into CLAUDE.md that loosens the 'No mocks' rule and was written outside the author's declared scope. Read that CLAUDE.md hunk against docs/testing-principles.md before merging to confirm it aligns rather than loosens.
